resources.string: Tells you a tab reached your relay
Tells you when a tab is waiting or couldn\'t be sent
Keeps the connection to your relay open so links arrive immediately
Connected to your relay, so links arrive immediately
Only get tabs when Tabsend is open

Tabs normally reach this phone right away, with no permanent notification and barely any battery cost. To do that, your relay asks the Tabsend wake-up service to ring this phone through Google, then this phone fetches the tab from your relay.
The wake-up service and Google learn that this phone received something, and when, and Google also sees the phone\'s internet address. They never learn what was sent or who sent it.
Turn this on if you\'d rather not share that. Tabs stay instant, but Android shows a permanent notification and Tabsend uses a little more battery.
Turn this on to stop that. Tabs will then arrive when you open Tabsend, or within a few minutes.
This is on, so tabs arrive when you open Tabsend, or within a few minutes. Turn it off to get them right away.

Pictures load directly from each website, so those sites can see this phone\'s internet address and when it asked.\n\nTurn this on if you don\'t want to be tracked this way. You\'ll see each site\'s first letter instead.
Tabsend is keeping a connection open itself, because you asked for no Google. Android shows a permanent notification while it does that.
Tabsend is keeping a connection open itself, because this phone has no Google services. Android shows a permanent notification while it does that.
Tabsend is keeping a connection open itself, because this version of the app does not use Google push. Android shows a permanent notification while it does that.
Tabsend is keeping a connection open itself, because your relay has no wake-up service set up. Android shows a permanent notification while it does that.
Tabsend is keeping a connection open itself for now. It will switch to Google\'s push service, and drop the notification, once it can reach it.

Tabsend is keeping a connection open itself, because wake-ups through Google stopped reaching this phone. Android shows a permanent notification while it does that. This usually means your relay rings a different wake-up service from the one this app signed up with, or that service is down. Once that is fixed, tap Try Google push again.
Could not switch back to Google push yet, because the wake-up service or your relay did not answer. Tabsend keeps its own connection open meanwhile.

Can\'t reach your relay at %1$s. It last answered %2$s, and sends are being held until it\'s back. This address only works on your home network. Away from home or on mobile data? Connect to your home Wi-Fi or turn on your VPN.
Linked. A newer Tabsend build is available (this app speaks v%1$s, the relay prefers v%2$s) — everything works, but it\'s worth updating.
This version of the Tabsend app is too old for that relay (app speaks v%1$s, relay needs v%2$s). Install the latest build, then pair again.
That relay is running an older version of Tabsend than this app (relay speaks v%1$s, app needs v%2$s). Update the relay, then pair again.

The relay answered, but its security certificate doesn\'t match the one in this setup link. If the relay was rebuilt or reinstalled it will have a new certificate — create a fresh setup link and scan it again.

The relay answered, but this phone doesn\'t trust its security certificate. The setup link did not include the certificate fingerprint this phone needs. Create a fresh link from the relay or an updated Tabsend device.

Android won\'t send plain http anywhere but localhost, so this address is blocked. The relay needs an https address — one with its own self-signed certificate is fine, as long as its setup link carries the fingerprint.

%1$s means this phone itself, so there\'s nothing there to reach. That address came from a relay that describes itself as localhost, which is a development-only setting. Give the relay a PUBLIC_RELAY_URL that other devices can reach, then create a new setup link.
